prerequisites: Basic knowledge in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and basics of Materials Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module know the essential manufacturing processes for plastics processing and understand what types of plastic products are produced with these processes. They also have broad knowledge of the physical principles of these processes, their problem areas, and possibilities for technical realization. They acquire the qualification to meet the requirements of the practical-oriented module Plastics Processing.

Successful graduates of this module possess in-depth knowledge regarding the relationships between material properties of plastics, processing methods and parameters, and the properties of the injected, extruded, thermoformed, or otherwise manufactured end product. They also have deepened knowledge, particularly concerning the effect of process parameters on product quality and economic efficiency, but also regarding tooling technology and environmental aspects such as resource conservation and recycling, for the two most widely used industrial plastics processing methods, injection molding and extrusion, and their special processes.

Students communicate and interact with each other and with the lecturers to understand, reflect on, and link plastics-related specialized knowledge. This is further deepened in the practical part through group work. Students can present work results orally and in writing in a structured form.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals in the interaction of plastics-specific and processing-technical properties and their influence on the quality of end products.
Processing methods for the production of plastic products (e.g., injection molding, extrusion, film production, stretching, thermoforming, and joining processes).
Practical part: practical introduction to plastics processing
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written examination. The ungraded assessment is experimental work in a group, consisting of approximately 10-15 pages.
